findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Concurrency behavior (RWMutex double-checked locking around a global cache) added without any test exercising concurrent access to GetWebAssets, so a data race or lock-ordering regression would ship undetected

[ADVISORY] Write path does not re-check entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock, allowing concurrent cold-start callers to each perform the full disk-walk asset scan, multiplying filesystem traversal work
[ADVISORY] Concurrency-fix (package-level RWMutex guarding global cache) is bundled into an optimization PR without a stated requirement — thread-safety remediation is untraceable to PR intent
[ADVISORY] Double-checked locking pattern serializes Dev path and non-Dev first-miss on the write lock across full asset loading including filesystem I/O
[ADVISORY] In Dev, GetWebAssets reloads from disk on every request and the mutex now serializes those reloads, turning concurrent Dev asset requests into a global serialization point
[ADVISORY] '// TODO: get rid of global state' comment carried into new var block with no tracked follow-up issue, shipping a knowingly under-scoped mechanism

[ADVISORY] Missing double-check after acquiring the write lock in pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:41-50: the read-lock check happens before the lock upgrade, so concurrent cold-start requests each take the write lock and re-run the full disk-scan asset load even when a prior holder already populated the cache

[ADVISORY] The write lock is held across the entire asset-load operation (recursive directory scan + disk I/O) in pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:47-49, so every concurrent GetWebAssets call blocks on the mutex while a slow/stalled filesystem read is in flight, with no timeout, potentially stalling all tenants' asset requests

[ADVISORY] Incomplete double-checked locking in webassets.go:40-47 — after RUnlock misses, the write lock is taken but the cache is never re-checked before rebuilding, so duplicate concurrent rebuilds serialize on the write lock and multiply cold-start latency

[ADVISORY] In webassets.go:32-35, the cached *dtos.EntryPointAssets pointer is shared across all callers with no copy-on-return, so any caller mutating the returned struct (e.g., trimming CSS/JS slices) corrupts the process-wide cache; the mutex protects the pointer slot but not the payload
Pre-existing global-state TODO comment (pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:36-38) is a code-smell concern, though not a security defect and predates the diff
Double-checked locking in GetWebAssets holds the write lock through the entire cache-miss path including filesystem reads, causing concurrent cache misses on cold start to serialize on the mutex

[ADVISORY] GetWebAssets returns the shared entryPointAssetsCache pointer directly to every caller without a copy or mutation-preventing interface; the mutex guards only the cache slot, not the object, so any caller mutating the returned *dtos.EntryPointAssets or nested shared slices causes a data race on a hot request path

[ADVISORY] The double-checked lock in webassets.go:43-48 is incomplete — no second entryPointAssetsCache != nil re-check after taking the write lock, so N concurrent cold-start requests each perform the full filesystem scan and overwrite the cache N times, causing a serialized stampede

[ADVISORY] In setting.Dev the write lock is held for the entire duration of on-disk asset discovery, serializing all asset requests on one mutex per process and causing head-of-line blocking while disk I/O runs

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Double-checked locking pattern serializes Dev path and non-Dev first-miss on the write lock across full asset loading including filesystem I/O

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an RWMutex and takes a write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(); defer Unlock()`) after the initial read-check. In `setting.Dev`, the cache is never returned (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil`), so every call will acquire and hold the write lock for the remainder of `GetWebAssets`, serializing concurrent requests. For non-Dev, the first cache miss also holds the write lock while the function computes `result`. The claim about filesystem I/O specifically isn’t shown in the snippet, but the serialization across the full remaining work is directly implied by the deferred unlock.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In Dev, GetWebAssets reloads from disk on every request and the mutex now serializes those reloads, turning concurrent Dev asset requests into a global serialization point

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and takes an exclusive `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` for all cache-miss paths. Since the early return is gated by `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`, Dev requests will always fall through and hit the exclusive lock, so concurrent Dev calls to `GetWebAssets` will be serialized through this mutex while reloading/building assets. This is a real diff-grounded performance/behavior concern in Dev, not a correctness defect.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a `// TODO: get rid of global state` comment next to the new global cache/mutex block, but the finding’s core claim—“with no tracked follow-up issue” and “shipping a knowingly under-scoped mechanism”—cannot be verified from the diff. The only concrete change shown is adding a mutex around an existing global cache; the presence/absence of issue tracking is outside what the diff demonstrates.

[ADVISORY] The write lock is held across the entire asset-load operation (recursive directory scan + disk I/O) in pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:47-49, so every concurrent GetWebAssets call blocks on the mutex while a slow/stalled filesystem read is in flight, with no timeout, potentially stalling all tenants' asset requests

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GetWebAssets` now takes a write lock (`entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` + `defer ...Unlock()`) immediately after the initial cache read, before any further work in the function. This means all concurrent callers will block on the write lock while the first caller performs the (unspecified here) asset-loading logic. The exact details of “recursive directory scan + disk I/O” aren’t shown in the snippet, but holding the write lock across the remainder of the function is verifiable and is a concrete contention/performance concern introduced by the change, not a correctness defect per se.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In webassets.go:32-35, the cached *dtos.EntryPointAssets pointer is shared across all callers with no copy-on-return, so any caller mutating the returned struct (e.g., trimming CSS/JS slices) corrupts the process-wide cache; the mutex protects the pointer slot but not the payload

adjudication.rationale: The diff still returns the cached *dtos.EntryPointAssets directly (now via `ret := entryPointAssetsCache` under an RLock) and does not clone/copy it before returning. The added RWMutex only serializes access to the cache slot (the pointer) and does not prevent callers from mutating the referenced struct after it’s returned. Whether any caller actually mutates it isn’t shown in this diff, so it’s a real design/robustness concern but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Double-checked locking in GetWebAssets holds the write lock through the entire cache-miss path including filesystem reads, causing concurrent cache misses on cold start to serialize on the mutex

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and on a cache miss takes `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` with `defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()`, meaning the write lock is held for the remainder of `GetWebAssets` (all work on the miss path). This will serialize concurrent callers during cold start/cache miss, regardless of what that work entails. The diff does not show the subsequent operations (e.g., filesystem reads), so the specific mention of filesystem reads isn’t directly verifiable here, but the broad serialization concern is grounded in the new locking structure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GetWebAssets returns the shared entryPointAssetsCache pointer directly to every caller without a copy or mutation-preventing interface; the mutex guards only the cache slot, not the object, so any caller mutating the returned *dtos.EntryPointAssets or nested shared slices causes a data race on a hot request path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GetWebAssets` returns the cached `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` pointer directly (`ret := entryPointAssetsCache` then `return ret, nil`) and the new `RWMutex` only protects reading/writing the cache pointer itself, not the contents of the pointed-to object. The finding’s claim about potential races if any caller mutates the returned struct (or nested slices/maps) is a plausible, diff-grounded concern, but the diff does not show any mutation by callers or that the object is actually mutated concurrently, so it’s not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The double-checked lock in webassets.go:43-48 is incomplete — no second entryPointAssetsCache != nil re-check after taking the write lock, so N concurrent cold-start requests each perform the full filesystem scan and overwrite the cache N times, causing a serialized stampede

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an RWMutex and does an initial read of `entryPointAssetsCache` under `RLock`, then unconditionally takes the write `Lock()` when the cache is nil / dev mode. There is no second `entryPointAssetsCache != nil` check after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent cold-start callers can each pass the initial nil read, queue on the write lock, and then redundantly execute the expensive asset-building path serially and overwrite the cache multiple times. This is a real, diff-grounded scalability/performance issue (stampede), but it doesn’t change correctness of the returned value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] In setting.Dev the write lock is held for the entire duration of on-disk asset discovery, serializing all asset requests on one mutex per process and causing head-of-line blocking while disk I/O runs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and, on any cache miss, unconditionally takes `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` with `defer Unlock()` before doing the rest of `GetWebAssets`. In `setting.Dev`, the early return is disabled (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && ret != nil`), so every call will acquire the write lock and then proceed into the (implied) on-disk asset discovery while holding it, serializing concurrent requests and causing head-of-line blocking during I/O. This is a performance/concurrency concern introduced by the change, not a correctness defect.
